categoryRules.description: First matching rule wins. Test runners, routing, setup, inventories, affected selection, coverage, and build-budget policy.
First matching rule wins. Mounted and browser-shaped ChatScreens behavior is visible chat/UI evidence, even when it invokes generation.
First matching rule wins. Settings, provider panels, Realm/catalog, and plugin/module authoring UI stay in the authoring category.
First matching rule wins. Authentication, authorization, egress and body limits, tracing, startup/shutdown, service workers, and platform routes.
First matching rule wins. Asset bytes and ownership, imports/exports, saves, backups, archive codecs, Realm staging, and historical formats.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed settings and plugin-storage range owners whose dominant contract is durable command mutation.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed module-editor draft storage whose dominant contract is browser recovery and writer isolation.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed plugin-provider response identity and provider-dashboard freshness owners whose dominant contract is provider request behavior.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed database analysis whose dominant contract is export materialization and asset ownership diagnostics.
First matching rule wins. Plugin/module permissions and lifecycle, MCP, RisuAccess, Playground, and developer-specialized tools.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed additional-HTML sanitization whose dominant contract is the platform untrusted-content boundary.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed partial-edit range projection whose dominant contract is visible editor behavior.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed output-trigger orchestration whose dominant contract is post-generation response processing.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed input-hook activity whose dominant contract is translation/provider request selection and accounting.
First matching rule wins. CBS, parsing, regex/display scripts, triggers, Lua, automation, and bounded execution.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed memory-named owners whose dominant contract is prompt and generation composition.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed embedding and summary adapter/model owners whose dominant contract is provider request behavior.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed stream-job registry and route owners whose dominant contract is shared runtime infrastructure.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed worker-error presentation whose dominant contract is visible application feedback.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed character-summary protocol projection whose dominant contract is browser state synchronization.
First matching rule wins. Memory, embeddings, summaries, ranking, jobs, queues, and worker lifecycle.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed parameter and character-emotion controls whose dominant contract is settings or character authoring.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed provider-list and completion-sound owners whose observable contract is mounted or visible UI.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed dispatch, emotion-processing, and client-context owners whose dominant contract is generation orchestration.
First matching rule wins. Provider adapters, models and credentials, translation, image/audio/transcription, and media codecs.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed prompt-named owners whose dominant contract is browser hydration and recovery.
First matching rule wins. Reviewed generation-settings and prompt-template owners whose dominant contract is durable mutation.
First matching rule wins. Prompt assembly, generation operations and effects, streaming, finalization, reroll, and Agent Presets.
First matching rule wins. Browser bootstrap, writer/observer state, outbox/replay, hydration, invalidation, refresh, and recovery.
First matching rule wins. SQLite persistence, revisions and receipts, commands/events, durable mutations, repositories, and editing bridges.
First matching rule wins. Settings UI, profiles, personas, characters, lorebook authoring, catalogs, loadouts, and reordering.
First matching rule wins. Navigation, visible chat behavior, sidebars, shared UI feedback, focus, accessibility, and responsive behavior.
A path unmatched above uses D when its resolved lane is built-browser or frontend-dom.
A path unmatched above uses L when its resolved lane is fastify-node.
Any remaining tracked frontend N/S path uses A and remains explicitly visible for Phase 1 review.
